questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The elements with the highest and the lowest enthalpy of atomisation respectively, for first row transition elements are:
questions.solution:
The enthalpy of atomisation is the enthalpy change that accompanies the total separation of all atoms in a chemical substance.

The extent of metallic bonding an element undergoes decides the enthalpy of atomization. The more extensive the metallic bonding of an element, the more will be its enthalpy of atomisation.

Sc has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation, for first row of transition elements and Zn (4d10 5s2) has completely filled d-orbital and has no unpaired electron to take part in the formation of metallic bonds. So, the metallic bonding in zinc is the weakest and it has the least enthalpy of atomisation.

Nitrates are difficult to reduce under the laboratory conditions but microbes do it easily. Ammonia forms large number of complexes with transition metal ions. Hybridisation easily explains the ease of sigma donation capability of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{PH}_3$. Phosphine is a flammable gas and is prepared from white phosphorus.Question: Among the following, the correct statement is
options: between $\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{PH}_3, \mathrm{NH}_3$ is a better electron donor because the lone pair of electrons occupies spherical 's' orbital and is less directional
between $\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{PH}_3, \mathrm{PH}_3$ is a better electron donor because the lone pair of electrons occupies $\mathrm{sp}^3$ orbital and is more directional
between $\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{PH}_3, \mathrm{NH}_3$ is a better electron donor because the lone pair of electrons occupies $\mathrm{sp}^3$ orbital and is more directional
between $\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{PH}_3, \mathrm{PH}_3$ is a better electron donor because the lone pair of electrons occupies spherical ' $s$ ' orbital and is less directional
questions.solution: $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is better electron donor because the lone pair of electrons occupies $\mathrm{sp}^3$-orbital and is more directional.

questions.q:
Match List I (substances) with List II (processes) employed in the manufacture of the substances and select the correct option

List I (Substances) List II (Processes)
1. Sulphuric acid (i) Haber's process
2. Steel (ii) Bessemer's process
3. Sodium hydroxide (iii) Leblanc process
4. Ammonia (iv) Contact process
questions.solution: Sulphuric acid is manufactured by contact process, steel is manufactured by Bessemer's process, Leblanc process is used for the production of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ while $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is obtained by Haber's process.

questions.solution: White phosphorus on reaction with limited supply of oxygen gives lower oxide $P_4 \mathrm{O}_6$. questions.q:
Referring to the following reactions the missing products A, B, C, and D respectively are

NH4Cl (aq) + NaNO2 (aq) → [A] + H2O (l)+ NaCl (aq)

NH 4 2 Cr 2 O 7   → Δ   B  +  H 2 O  l +  Cr 2 O 3   s

Cu + HNO3 (dilute) → Cu(NO3)2 + [C] + H2O(l)  

Cu + HNO3 (concentrate) → Cu(NO3)2 + [D] + H2O(l)
questions.solution:
(i) In the laboratory, dinitrogen is prepared by treating an aqueous solution of ammonium chloride with sodium nitrite.

NH 4 Cl aq + NaNO 2 aq → N 2 g +2 H 2 O l +NaCl aq

Small amounts of NO and HNO 3 are also formed as impurities, which can be removed by passing the gas through aqueous sulphuric acid containing potassium dichromate.

(ii) Dinitrogen can also be prepared by heating ammonium dichromate

NH 4 2 Cr 2 O 7 s ⟶ Δ N 2 (g) + 4H 2 O l⁡ + Cr 2 O 3 s

(iii) Copper metal reacts with dilute HNO 3 to form nitrogen (II) oxide NO

3Cus+8HNO3 dilute→ 3CuNO32aq +2NOg+4H2Ol

(iv) Copper metal reacts with conc. HNO 3 to form nitrogen (IV) oxide or nitrogen dioxide NO 2 .

Cu( s ) +4HNO 3 ( conc. )→Cu ( NO 3 ) 2 ( aq ) +2NO 2 ( g ) +2H 2 O( l )
